methods.name: initialize
methods.doc: Negotiate the protocol version and exchange identity. Must be the first request on a connection, and is the only one accepted before Ready.

methods.name: session.list
methods.doc: Read a bounded daemon-ordered session-index page.

methods.name: session.create
methods.doc: Create a new session.

methods.name: session.patch
methods.doc: Patch session settings.

methods.name: session.remove
methods.doc: Remove a session and its data.

methods.name: session.fork
methods.doc: Fork a session from another session's transcript.

methods.name: session.compact
methods.doc: Request manual compaction of the transcript context.

methods.name: session.rewind
methods.doc: Truncate the transcript at a user message.

methods.name: session.send_input
methods.doc: Send user input to a session.

methods.name: session.cancel_input

methods.name: session.cancel_run

methods.name: session.history

methods.name: permission.decide

methods.name: session.config

methods.name: subscription.set

methods.name: catalog.list

methods.name: catalog.refresh

methods.name: workspace.describe

methods.name: workspace.browse
methods.doc: List directories on the daemon host.

methods.name: workspace.remove

methods.name: workspace.skills

methods.name: permission.rules
methods.doc: List remembered permission rules for a workspace.

methods.name: permission.forget
methods.doc: Forget a remembered permission rule.

methods.name: cron.create

methods.name: cron.patch

methods.name: cron.list

methods.name: cron.run_now

errors.doc: Request was syntactically or semantically invalid.
Wire-level framing / version violation.
Unknown RPC method name.
Session id does not exist.
Workspace id does not exist.
A paged-query cursor names an invalidated result generation.
Message id does not exist in this session.
Part index is out of range for the parent message.
Input id does not exist or was already consumed.
`config_rev` is not the session's current revision.
Job id does not exist.
A run is already active on the target job.
Skill name is unknown to this daemon.

The run the request targets is not the current run.
Permission descriptor or prompt id is unknown.

Session is busy and cannot accept the request right now.
Session has persistent children and removal did not request a cascade.
Underlying runtime (model / tool) failed.
Patch failed structural or content validation.
Model id is not supported by this daemon.
Reasoning effort is not supported by the selected model.
Catch-all for unspecified internal errors.
Retry this request after backoff; the connection stays up, only this request was shed. Client behavior: exponential-backoff re-send of the same request.

fields.name: seq
fields.doc: Sequence number on the durable stream.

fields.name: timing

fields.name: seq
fields.doc: Sequence number on the durable stream.

fields.doc: Sequence number on the durable stream.

fields.name: part_id

fields.name: permission_state

structures.name: Model_Cost

structures.name: Model_Info

fields.name: context_window

fields.name: max_output_tokens

fields.name: reasoning_levels

structures.name: Skipped_Provider

fields.name: message

fields.name: session

fields.name: input

fields.name: next_run_ms

fields.name: last_run_ms

fields.name: last_session_id

structures.name: Request
structures.doc: Client request frame with typed method params.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: Correlation id, echoed verbatim in the response.

structures.name: Response_Ok
structures.doc: Successful server response; carries the typed method result.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: Correlation id copied from the request.

fields.name: result
fields.doc: Method result, tagged by the request method that produced it.

structures.name: Response_Error
structures.doc: Failed server response; carries a method-agnostic error object.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: Correlation id copied from the request.

structures.name: Notification
structures.doc: Server-pushed notification: a request object with no `id`, so nothing replies. Ordering, replay, gating, and droppability are ours — see `broadcast_name_class`, `Seq`, and `session.resync`.

fields.name: method
fields.doc: Broadcast name, occupying the same `method` namespace as requests.

fields.name: protocol
fields.doc: Protocol version this client speaks. Must equal `PROTOCOL_VERSION`.

fields.name: server_now_ms
fields.doc: Daemon wall-clock epoch ms at initialize time.

structures.name: Initialize_Result
structures.doc: Result of the `initialize` request: the coarse daemon snapshot.

fields.name: session_revision
fields.doc: Current compact session-index revision for this connection generation.

fields.name: cron_revision
fields.doc: Current cron-index revision for this connection generation.

fields.name: capabilities
fields.doc: Optional daemon surfaces this build/config advertises; see `Capability`.

structures.name: Skill_Ref
structures.doc: A named skill invocation with its rendered arguments. Shared by `Input_Skill` and `User_Message.skill`.

structures.name: Queued_Input
structures.doc: A queued input waiting behind an active turn.

fields.name: run_id
fields.doc: Run started to handle this input.

fields.name: run_id
fields.doc: Specific run to cancel; omit to cancel the active run.

fields.name: canceled_run
fields.doc: Run that was canceled; null if none was active.

fields.name: cleared_compaction
fields.doc: Compaction run canceled alongside; null if none was active.

structures.name: Part_Delta
structures.doc: Incremental text/reasoning bytes for a draft. `offset` is UTF-8 bytes already present: == len appends, < len is a no-op, > len is a gap (call session.resync).

fields.name: offset
fields.doc: UTF-8 bytes already applied on the receiver.

structures.name: Empty
structures.doc: Empty params/result object (`{}`) for methods whose registry entry uses `{}`. One type for both directions: an empty object carries no direction-specific meaning.

structures.name: Session_Result
structures.doc: Result of `session.create`, `session.fork`, and `session.patch`. The returned session carries the resulting config_rev and permission mode.

structures.name: Notice
structures.doc: Daemon diagnostic notice broadcast to all connections. Non-owning.

structures.name: Permission_Option
structures.doc: One option the daemon proposes for a permission request.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: Stable option key clients echo back.

fields.name: creates
fields.doc: Rule shapes produced when chosen (for `allow_always`); each element @bounded 512.

structures.name: Permission_Decision_User
structures.doc: Decided by a user selecting an option.

structures.name: Permission_Decision_Rule
structures.doc: Decided by a matched persisted rule.

structures.name: Permission_State
structures.doc: Local-only lifecycle data folded into tool state. Never a broadcast.

fields.name: requested_at_ms
fields.doc: When the daemon issued the prompt.

fields.name: options
fields.doc: Options offered to the user. Absent for rule-resolved decisions; at most 32.

structures.name: Permission_Rule
structures.doc: A remembered "allow always" answer, scoped to a workspace.

fields.name: session_id
fields.doc: If non-null, rule is scoped to one session.

fields.name: tool
fields.doc: Tool name this rule applies to.

fields.name: action
fields.doc: Allow or deny the matched call.

fields.name: message_id
fields.doc: Message the permission prompt belongs to.

fields.name: part_id
fields.doc: Part the permission prompt belongs to.

fields.name: message
fields.doc: Client-supplied reason, meaningful only when option_id resolves to a reject kind; the daemon routes it into Tool_State_Denied.reason.

fields.name: rules
fields.doc: Remembered rules for the requested workspace.

structures.name: Run_Canceled_Timing
structures.doc: Cancellation timing; an accepted queued run may never start.

fields.name: started_at_ms
fields.doc: Start epoch ms, or null when canceled before starting.

structures.name: Token_Usage
structures.doc: Token accounting for one assistant message.

structures.name: Run_Outcome_Turn
structures.doc: A completed turn: it stopped for a stop reason after some round trips.

fields.name: rounds
fields.doc: Number of model/tool round trips used.

structures.name: Run_Outcome_Compacted
structures.doc: A manual compaction that produced a summary.

structures.name: Run_Outcome_Skipped
structures.doc: A manual compaction that did nothing.

structures.name: Run_Outcome_Canceled
structures.doc: A run canceled by the user or daemon. Its timing rides the terminal envelope.

structures.name: Run_Outcome_Failed
structures.doc: A run that failed after daemon retry policy was exhausted.

structures.name: System_Prompt_Default
structures.doc: Request-time system prompt override; the default arm means the field was omitted.

structures.name: Max_Rounds_Default
structures.doc: Request-time max-rounds override; the default arm means the field was omitted.

fields.name: workspace_path
fields.doc: Filesystem path; omitted resolves to the home directory.

fields.name: profile
fields.doc: Profile name to resolve config from.

fields.name: system_prompt
fields.doc: Omitted = resolve from config. Explicit null = force no system prompt.

structures.name: Session_Patch
structures.doc: Missing field means no change. The system prompt is snapshotted at creation and is not patchable. Non-owning.

fields.name: before_message_id
fields.doc: Fork up to (exclusive); omit to fork the full transcript.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: Whether compaction started or was queued.

fields.name: parent_message_id
fields.doc: Message in the parent's transcript carrying the spawning tool part.

fields.name: parent_part_id
fields.doc: Tool part within that message that spawned this session; together with `parent_message_id` stays correct when one message emits multiple spawn calls.

fields.name: max_rounds
fields.doc: Live round cap; null means unlimited.

fields.name: created_at_ms
fields.doc: Creation epoch ms. Never changes; `updated_at_ms` is never below it.

fields.name: created_by
fields.doc: Client that created the session; null for daemon-created child/cron sessions.

fields.name: agent
fields.doc: Agent name, when known; omitted if unassigned. Lets a client listing children name the agent without fetching a transcript.

fields.name: config_rev
fields.doc: Config revision used by the run.

fields.name: config
fields.doc: Config the named run is executing under. Present exactly when `state` names a run that has one; absent under `idle` and `compacting`.

fields.name: queued
fields.doc: Accepted inputs waiting to run. At most LIMITS.max_queued_inputs.

structures.name: Session_List_Item
structures.doc: Full compact row returned by session.list and session-index broadcasts. Non-owning; nested slices share the containing frame arena.

fields.name: activity
fields.doc: Current coarse activity; idle is explicit.

structures.name: Session_Scope_Workspace
structures.doc: Sessions belonging to one exact workspace.

structures.name: Session_Population_Top_Level
structures.doc: User-facing conversations: root sessions and forks.

structures.name: Session_Population_Children
structures.doc: Immediate persistent children of one session.

structures.name: Session_Population_Job_Runs
structures.doc: Sessions created by one cron job.

fields.name: scope
fields.doc: Workspace scope; omitted means no workspace restriction.

fields.name: population
fields.doc: Relationship population; omitted means user-facing top-level sessions.

fields.name: view
fields.doc: Membership and ordering; omitted means active_recent.

fields.name: limit
fields.doc: Page size; omitted means daemon default.

fields.name: revision
fields.doc: Compact-index revision represented by every field in this result.

fields.name: items
fields.doc: Rows in final daemon-defined display order.

fields.name: next_cursor
fields.doc: Opaque continuation; required null on the final page.

fields.name: total
fields.doc: Unique rows in the complete selected view before paging.

structures.name: Activity_State_Building
structures.doc: Runtime is being built as the first phase of a run.

fields.name: started_at_ms
fields.doc: Run and build start epoch ms.

fields.name: limit
fields.doc: Max messages to return; omit for daemon default.

structures.name: Active_Draft
structures.doc: In-flight assistant draft, resent on resync. Non-owning.

structures.name: Session_Resync_Result
structures.doc: Full session snapshot for reconnection. Non-owning.

fields.name: item
fields.doc: Current compact session-index row at this snapshot cut.

fields.name: base_seq
fields.doc: Sequence number to resume the durable stream from.

fields.name: highest_finalized_message_id
fields.doc: Highest message id already committed or discarded at the snapshot cut. Required on the wire; null when no message has finalized.

fields.name: queued
fields.doc: Inputs queued behind the active turn.

fields.name: limit
fields.doc: Max messages to return; omit for daemon default.

fields.name: has_more
fields.doc: Whether older messages exist beyond this page.

fields.name: config_rev
fields.doc: Specific revision to fetch; omit for the live config.

fields.name: system_prompt
fields.doc: null means no system prompt is sent to the model.

fields.name: sessions
fields.doc: Sessions to subscribe to; replaces the prior set.

structures.name: Message_Time
structures.doc: Creation/completion timestamps on an assistant message.

fields.name: completed_at_ms
fields.doc: Completion epoch ms; null while still in flight.

structures.name: Created_Time
structures.doc: Creation timestamp on a user or compaction message. These message kinds carry `{ created_at_ms }` only — no `completed_at_ms` (that is assistant-only).

structures.name: Message_Error
structures.doc: Structured error on an assistant message with `finish: "error"`. Non-owning.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: Part ordinal in the message content array.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: Part ordinal in the message content array.

fields.name: signature
fields.doc: Opaque provider data: Anthropic's extended-thinking block signature, delivered by `signature_delta`. Empty when the provider issued none. Persisted verbatim and replayed verbatim on the next request of a tool-use conversation; never interpreted. A part carrying one must never be collapsed or reordered by a normalization pass, even when `text` is empty: the signature covers the block at its position.

structures.name: Redacted_Reasoning_Part
structures.doc: Opaque safety-redacted model reasoning payload. Non-owning.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: Part ordinal in the message content array.

fields.name: data
fields.doc: Opaque encrypted provider data. Persist and replay it verbatim at this position; never interpret, normalize, collapse, or reorder it.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: Part ordinal in the message content array.

fields.name: call_id
fields.doc: Provider identity; never used to address the part.

fields.name: permission_state
fields.doc: Local permission lifecycle. Absent under `pending`; options-and-no-decision under `waiting_permission`; decided when present, except under `canceled`.

fields.name: output
fields.doc: Accumulated display output streamed so far. Present in a resync snapshot of a running tool, absent in the live transition into `running`. Its UTF-8 byte length is the next `tool.output_delta` offset baseline.

fields.name: duration_ms
fields.doc: Null when the call never started running.

fields.name: input_id
fields.doc: The accepted input this message came from (client- or daemon-minted).

fields.name: skill
fields.doc: Skill this message's rendered body came from, if any.

structures.name: Turn_Provenance
structures.doc: Which provider actually produced one assistant turn. Absent on a turn the daemon built before the field existed. `Assistant_Message.config_rev` records the configuration a turn was *requested* under and can be resolved away by a later config change; this records what answered, which is what makes provider-scoped opaque data (a reasoning part's signature) safe to replay: replay it only when the next request goes to the same protocol and model. Non-owning.

fields.name: protocol
fields.doc: Protocol the turn was produced under.

fields.name: model
fields.doc: Model id that produced the turn, resolved at request time.

fields.name: config_rev
fields.doc: Resolves to a model string via session.config or config.changed.

fields.name: agent
fields.doc: Agent name (`"main"` for a root session).

fields.name: finish
fields.doc: Present on every committed message; absent on a draft.

fields.name: provenance
fields.doc: Provider that produced this turn; absent on turns older than the field.

fields.name: summary
fields.doc: Model-generated summary of the dropped range.

fields.name: first_kept_id
fields.doc: First message id still in the provider context. Null means nothing was kept.

structures.name: Diff_Hunk
structures.doc: One hunk of a unified diff.

fields.name: lines
fields.doc: Hunk body, one line per element (no trailing newlines). Owner: caller/arena.

structures.name: Diff_File
structures.doc: One file in a diff view.

fields.name: old_path
fields.doc: Path in the old tree when the file was renamed.

fields.name: hunks
fields.doc: Per-file hunks in file order. Owner: caller/arena.

fields.name: files
fields.doc: Files in the diff. Owner: caller/arena.

structures.name: Git_Info
structures.doc: Git status for a workspace root, when it is a repo. Non-owning.

fields.name: dirty
fields.doc: Whether the working tree has uncommitted changes.

fields.name: git
fields.doc: Git status; null when the root is not a repo.

fields.name: last_used_model
fields.doc: Last model used in this workspace; null if never run.

fields.name: limit
fields.doc: Page size; omitted means daemon default.

fields.name: cursor
fields.doc: Opaque continuation within the same directory.

structures.name: Dir_Entry
structures.doc: A single filesystem entry in a browse listing. Non-owning.

fields.name: is_git_repo
fields.doc: Whether this directory is itself a git repo.

fields.name: parent
fields.doc: Parent directory path; null at the filesystem root.

fields.name: next_cursor
fields.doc: Opaque continuation; required null on the final page.

structures.name: Workspace_Ref
structures.doc: Params naming a workspace and nothing else. Shared by `workspace.remove`, `workspace.skills`, and `permission.rules`; split it the moment one of them needs a field of its own.

fields.name: related_job_ids
fields.doc: Cron jobs that referenced the removed workspace.

unions.name: Broadcast_Data
unions.doc: Typed broadcast payload, tagged by broadcast name on the frame. A broadcast frame's data is always exactly one of these variants.

unions.name: Catalog_List_Result
unions.doc: Result of catalog.list: unchanged since `since_rev`, or a full catalog snapshot.

unions.name: Skip_Reason
unions.doc: Reason a provider was skipped.

unions.name: Media_Source
unions.doc: Where media bytes live. Inline (base64) capped at LIMITS.max_inline_media_bytes; blob is a content hash fetched over HTTP.

unions.name: Content_Part
unions.doc: One piece of user or model content. Non-owning.

unions.name: Cron_Schedule
unions.doc: A cron schedule: recurring or one-shot. Non-owning.

unions.name: Response
unions.doc: Server response frame. One frame shape carrying exactly one of `result` / `error`; the outcome is which member is present.

unions.name: Input
unions.doc: A unit of user input: either raw content or a skill invocation. Non-owning.

unions.name: Session_Send_Input_Result
unions.doc: Result of `session.send_input`: started immediately or queued behind an active turn.

unions.name: Request_Params
unions.doc: Runtime params payload tagged by the same enum as `Method_Name`.

unions.name: Response_Result
unions.doc: Runtime result payload tagged by the request method that produced it.

unions.name: Permission_Decision
unions.doc: Who answered a permission request, and how. Non-owning.

unions.name: Run_Outcome
unions.doc: A run's terminal outcome, discriminated by `type`. Cancellation and failure are terminal outcomes here (folded in from the former run.canceled / run.failed).

unions.name: System_Prompt_Override
unions.doc: Request-time system prompt override. `default` means the field was omitted.

unions.name: Max_Rounds_Override
unions.doc: Request-time max-rounds override. `default` means the field was omitted.

unions.name: Session_Origin
unions.doc: How a session was created.

unions.name: Session_Scope
unions.doc: Workspace scope searched by session.list.

unions.name: Session_Population
unions.doc: Session relationship population searched by session.list.

unions.name: Activity_State
unions.doc: Session activity variant. The `message_id`, `part_id`, and `tool_name` locators are deliberately derivable: they are a checksum, and disagreement is a client's cue to resync.

unions.name: Assistant_Part
unions.doc: One element of an assistant message `content[]`. Non-owning.

unions.name: Tool_State
unions.doc: Lifecycle state of a tool part. Non-owning.

unions.name: Message
unions.doc: A transcript message. Non-owning.

unions.name: View
unions.doc: Display-only rendering hint. Frontends may render natively or ignore. Non-owning.

values.doc: Permission for this prompt was already decided.

values.name: Session_Busy
values.doc: Session is busy and cannot accept the request right now.

values.name: Session_Has_Children
values.doc: Session has persistent children and removal did not request a cascade.

values.name: Invalid_Patch
values.doc: Patch failed structural or content validation.

values.name: Unsupported_Model
values.doc: Model id is not supported by this daemon.

values.name: Unsupported_Reasoning
values.doc: Reasoning effort is not supported by the selected model.

values.name: Overloaded
values.doc: Retry this request after backoff; the connection stays up, only this request was shed. Client behavior: exponential-backoff re-send of the same request.

enumerations.name: Run_Error_Code
enumerations.doc: Why a run failed after daemon retry policy was exhausted.

values.name: Provider
values.doc: Provider rejected or failed the request.

values.name: Protocol
values.doc: Provider stream could not be parsed.

enumerations.name: Cron_Retain
enumerations.doc: Whether a fired session should be retained after the run ends.

values.name: On_Failure
values.doc: Keep only if the run failed.

enumerations.name: Cron_Overlap
enumerations.doc: Behavior when a new fire overlaps an active run.

enumerations.name: Cron_Missed_Policy
enumerations.doc: What to do with a fire missed while offline / behind.

values.name: Run_Once
values.doc: Run once immediately on recovery, then resume the schedule.

enumerations.name: Cron_Run_Outcome
enumerations.doc: Outcome tag for a single cron fire.

values.name: Dispatch_Failed
values.doc: Daemon could not dispatch the fire (e.g. workspace busy).

enumerations.name: Capability
enumerations.doc: Optional daemon surface a client may probe for. This is the ONE enum decoded tolerantly: an unknown capability string is IGNORED, never a Validation_Error. Tolerant decode is the whole point — a newer daemon advertises a token an older client does not know, and the client must skip it, not reject the frame. Every other enum in this package hard-rejects an unknown value; this one must not.

enumerations.name: Method_Name
enumerations.doc: Closed enum of RPC method names. Source of truth for the method set.

values.name: Initialize
values.doc: Negotiate the protocol version and exchange identity. Must be the first request on a connection, and is the only one accepted before Ready.

values.name: Session_List
values.doc: Read a bounded daemon-ordered session-index page.

values.name: Session_Remove
values.doc: Remove a session and its data.

values.name: Session_Fork
values.doc: Fork a session from another session's transcript.

values.name: Session_Compact
values.doc: Request manual compaction of the transcript context.

values.name: Session_Rewind
values.doc: Truncate the transcript at a user message.

values.name: Session_Send_Input
values.doc: Send user input to a session.

values.name: Session_Cancel_Input
values.doc: Cancel a queued input that has not started.

values.name: Session_Cancel_Run
values.doc: Cancel the active run, optionally clearing queue and pending compaction.

values.name: Session_Resync
values.doc: Resync a session with a windowed transcript snapshot.

values.name: Session_History
values.doc: Read older committed history beyond the resync window.

values.name: Session_Config
values.doc: Fetch a session's run config and system prompt by config_rev.

values.name: Catalog_List
values.doc: Fetch the model catalog, with optional `since_rev`.

values.name: Catalog_Refresh
values.doc: Re-read provider and credential configuration from disk.

values.name: Workspace_Describe
values.doc: Describe an arbitrary path as a workspace.

values.name: Workspace_Browse
values.doc: List directories on the daemon host.

values.name: Workspace_Remove
values.doc: Remove a workspace and its sessions.

values.name: Workspace_Skills
values.doc: List skills available in a workspace.

values.name: Permission_Rules
values.doc: List remembered permission rules for a workspace.

enumerations.name: Notice_Level
enumerations.doc: Severity of a daemon diagnostic notice.

enumerations.name: Permission_Option_Kind
enumerations.doc: Kinds of options the daemon may propose on a permission prompt.

values.name: Allow_Once
values.doc: Allow once for this call only.

values.name: Allow_Session
values.doc: Allow for the rest of the session.

values.name: Allow_Always
values.doc: Persist as a workspace rule and allow.

values.name: Reject_Always
values.doc: Persist a deny rule and reject; its `creates` patterns produce deny rules (mirror of Allow_Always).

enumerations.name: Denied_By
enumerations.doc: Who or what denied a tool call.

values.name: User
values.doc: A user selected a reject option.

values.name: Policy
values.doc: Daemon policy rejected the call without prompting.

enumerations.name: Rule_Action
enumerations.doc: Whether a remembered permission rule allows or denies the matched call.

enumerations.name: Run_Kind
enumerations.doc: What kind of run occupies a session.

values.name: Turn
values.doc: User-driven round of model + tool calls.

enumerations.name: Compact_Skip_Reason
enumerations.doc: Why a manual compaction did nothing.

values.name: Too_Few_Messages
values.doc: Too few messages to summarize meaningfully.

enumerations.name: Stop_Reason
enumerations.doc: Why a message stopped.

values.name: Length
values.doc: Hit the model's max-output token limit.

values.name: Tool_Calls
values.doc: Stopped to run one or more tool calls.

values.name: Unknown
values.doc: Stop reason did not map to a known value.

enumerations.name: Compact_Status
enumerations.doc: Whether compaction started immediately or was queued.

enumerations.name: Permission_Mode
enumerations.doc: Permission policy for future tool calls.

enumerations.name: Session_View
enumerations.doc: Closed daemon-defined session-list ordering.

enumerations.name: Compaction_Reason
enumerations.doc: Why compaction is running.

enumerations.name: Provider_Protocol
enumerations.doc: Provider request/response protocol a turn was produced under. Closed set; the transport picks a decoder from it, and persisted provenance names it so a later replay can tell whether opaque provider data still applies.

enumerations.name: Skill_Scope
enumerations.doc: Where a skill definition was loaded from.

aliases.name: Message_Part_Delta_Data
aliases.doc: Payload for `message.part_delta`: incremental draft bytes folded by UTF-8 offset.

aliases.name: Tool_Output_Delta_Data
aliases.doc: Payload for `tool.output_delta`: incremental display output for a running tool part, offset-folded like `message.part_delta` but targeting the tool output stream.

aliases.name: Session_Id
aliases.doc: 16 lowercase hex chars. Doubles as an on-disk directory name.

aliases.name: Workspace_Id
aliases.doc: 16 lowercase hex chars. Doubles as an on-disk directory name.

aliases.name: Job_Id
aliases.doc: 16 lowercase hex chars. Doubles as an on-disk record name.

aliases.name: Rule_Id
aliases.doc: 16 lowercase hex chars. Identifies one remembered permission rule.

aliases.name: Request_Id
aliases.doc: Correlation id as its verbatim JSON token — `7`, `"abc"` with quotes, or `null`. Opaque: JSON-RPC requires the response id to equal the request id.

aliases.name: Message_Id
aliases.doc: Session-scoped, daemon-minted, strictly increasing, never reused.

aliases.name: Run_Id
aliases.doc: Session-scoped, daemon-minted, strictly increasing, never reused.

aliases.name: Input_Id
aliases.doc: Session-scoped, daemon-minted, strictly increasing, never reused.

aliases.name: Part_Id
aliases.doc: Part ordinal in message.content[], from 0. JSON number on the wire, like the other session-scoped ids.

aliases.name: Seq
aliases.doc: Per-session monotonic sequence number on durable broadcasts.

aliases.name: Session_Revision
aliases.doc: Monotonic compact-session-index revision within one daemon lifetime.

aliases.name: Cron_Revision
aliases.doc: Monotonic cron-index revision within one daemon lifetime.

aliases.name: Config_Rev
aliases.doc: Monotonic run-config revision within a session.
